references.text: Abraham fears for his life because of his wife Sarai and asks her to say she is his sister, showing the same pattern of fear of being killed.
Isaac repeats his father's action by lying about his wife Rebekah out of fear that the men of the place would kill him—a pattern that mirrors Abraham's fear and actions.
Psalm 36:2 describes the wicked as having no fear of God, which reflects Abraham's concern about the lack of reverence for God in the place where he was staying.
Joseph says 'I fear God' as the basis for righteous action—a contrast to Abraham's fear that there was no fear of God in Gerar.
'The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge'—a central verse about reverence for God as a moral foundation, the same theme Abraham points to in his reasoning.
